name: Question 11
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083350/assets/58076d96d149ff4521103fd15c7187bc1a58595ab20f28be92be0f79385aee61.png)

Find the parametric equations of the line shown in the figure above.
worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the points $P(-1,1,4)$ and $Q(3,-2,2).$ Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$,  as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -3t \\ -2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1+4t \\ 1-3t \\ 4-2t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1+4t \\ y=1-3t \\ z=4-2t\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

Find the parametric equations of the line shown in the figure above.

a
{x=4−ty=−3+tz=−2+4t
b
{x=3−ty=−2+tz=2+4t
c
{x=4ty=−3tz=−2t
d
{x=−1+4ty=1−3tz=4−2t
e
{x=−ty=tz=4t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We know that the line passes through the points P(−1,1,4) and Q(3,−2,2). Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector PQ→, as follows:

v=PQ→=OQ→−OP→=[3−22]−[−114]=[4−3−2]

So, the vector equation of the line is

r=p+tvr=[−114]+t[4−3−2][xyz]=[−114]+[4t−3t−2t][xyz]=[−1+4t1−3t4−2t],

where t∈(−∞,∞). Therefore, the parametric equations are: {x=−1+4ty=1−3tz=4−2t
